interest: This document highlights early 1930s administrative and security concerns regarding Japanese agricultural colonization and landholding in Davao, Mindanao—a region where large Japanese hemp plantations and settlements generated local tension and scrutiny. Although preserved here as a cross-reference sheet, it demonstrates the intelligence sharing and coordination between the insular government of the Philippines, the U.S. War Department's Bureau of Insular Affairs, and the State Department over the strategic implications of Japanese migration within U.S. territory.
overview: This file contains a single Department of State document file sheet (cross-reference sheet) dated August 15, 1930, catalogued under decimal file 894.56118/3 regarding Japanese emigration to the Philippine Islands. The sheet cross-references a confidential letter from the War Department (filed under 811b.5594/orig) which quotes a confidential report sent to the Bureau of Insular Affairs by the Governor of the Philippine Islands. The underlying communication concerns growing local agitation and unrest in the Province of Davao on the island of Mindanao prompted by the increasing numbers and activities of Japanese settlers.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a confidential War Department letter regarding unrest in Davao over Japanese migration.
subfiles.summary: A Department of State document file sheet dated August 15, 1930, cross-referencing a confidential letter from the War Department filed under 811b.5594/orig. The underlying letter conveys a confidential report from the Governor of the Philippine Islands to the Bureau of Insular Affairs. The report details local agitation and unrest in Davao Province, Mindanao, surrounding the rising number of Japanese residents and their expanding activities.
